answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 9 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The garden multiplier is published, charged in onyx, and atlas lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2434 identities would post 949 proofs and burn roughly 61 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
